question: Should OpenClaw core permanently own a repeatable ordered-config CLI contract with earlier-layer authority and a read-only Gateway lifetime?
rationale: Tests and runtime proof can establish implementation quality, but they cannot decide whether core should expose and maintain this new configuration lifecycle instead of leaving composition and policy ownership to launchers or the RFC process.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded core mode
options.body: Accept the generic startup-only contract, then require a current-main rebase and fresh-install plus upgrade validation before merge.

options.title: Keep layering outside core
options.body: Reject the new CLI contract and continue the design in the linked RFC or launcher while using existing `$include` and validation surfaces where sufficient.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded core mode
recommendation.body: Accept the generic startup-only contract, then require a current-main rebase and fresh-install plus upgrade validation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice establishes a foundational core configuration and managed-hosting product contract rather than a mechanical code repair.
